# Best portable power station for camping

The best pick depends on how much you need to run. For most campers, a small 250-300Wh unit is enough, and a 1,000Wh+ unit makes sense if you're running a fridge or staying several nights.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb) is PowerStationGearLab's top pick for light weight and simplicity. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you'll find the Plus through Amazon and other retailers. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC) is the better value if you want more AC output, and it can expand to 572Wh. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard version with an AC outlet, not the "DC" variant. Note that OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored it only 50/100, so it's a budget pick. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** (288Wh, 600W) is TechRadar's budget pick. [Source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Multi-day trips, electric cooler, or van/overland
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping (scored 81/100). It's about 39 lb with 2,200W output and is on sale for under $900 (list $1,499). [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's camping pick. It's about $1,079, 1,536Wh, IP65 rated, and just under 40 lb. [Source](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh) is TechRadar's camping pick and PowerStationGearLab's van pick. [Source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's best value (under $530 on sale), though its fan is noisy. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180** ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, 1,152Wh, 1,800W) suits weekend trips and power tools. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, and the code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

## My recommendation
- **Just phones, lights, and a CPAP:** get a 288Wh unit like the Jackery 300 Plus or EcoFlow River 3 Plus. Turn off the CPAP humidifier, since it can triple the power draw.
- **Cooler, fan, and laptop for several days:** get the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, or the Anker C1000 Gen 2 if you want to spend less.

## Caveats
- Most of these sources earn affiliate commissions, so prices and "best" labels vary. I only have exact buy links for the AC180. For the others, the review pages above have the retailer buttons, and you should check the current price at checkout.
- A solar panel (Jackery's SolarSaga works well with its units) helps on trips longer than a weekend.
- None of these can go on a plane, since they exceed the 100Wh limit.

Tell me your budget and what you plan to power, and I can narrow it to one pick.
